bone.frontal_bone.name: Frontal bone
bone.frontal_bone.summary: Forms the forehead, the roofs of the orbits and most of the anterior cranial fossa. Contains the frontal sinuses.

bone.parietal_bone.name: Parietal bone
bone.parietal_bone.summary: Paired bones forming the sides and roof of the cranial vault; they meet in the midline at the sagittal suture.

bone.occipital_bone.name: Occipital bone
bone.occipital_bone.summary: Forms the back and much of the base of the skull. Surrounds the foramen magnum; its occipital condyles articulate with the atlas (C1).

bone.temporal_bone.name: Temporal bone
bone.temporal_bone.summary: Houses the middle and inner ear. Bears the mandibular fossa of the temporomandibular joint, and the mastoid, styloid and zygomatic processes.
bone.temporal_bone.clinical: Its thin squamous part at the pterion overlies the middle meningeal artery.

bone.sphenoid_bone.name: Sphenoid bone
bone.sphenoid_bone.summary: Central bone of the skull base. Its sella turcica holds the pituitary gland; its wings and pterygoid processes give passage and attachment to many nerves and muscles.
bone.sphenoid_bone.clinical: The pituitary gland sits in its sella turcica.

bone.ethmoid_bone.name: Ethmoid bone
bone.ethmoid_bone.summary: Light, air-filled bone between the orbits. Its cribriform plate transmits olfactory nerve fibres; it forms part of the nasal septum and the superior and middle nasal conchae.
bone.ethmoid_bone.clinical: Fracture of the cribriform plate can cause loss of smell and leakage of cerebrospinal fluid from the nose.

bone.maxilla.name: Maxilla
bone.maxilla.summary: The upper jaw. Holds the upper teeth and forms the floor of the orbit, part of the hard palate and the lateral wall of the nasal cavity. Contains the maxillary sinus.
bone.maxilla.clinical: Mid-face fractures are classified by the Le Fort system.

bone.zygomatic_bone.name: Zygomatic bone
bone.zygomatic_bone.summary: The cheekbone. Forms the prominence of the cheek and part of the lateral orbital wall; with the temporal bone it forms the zygomatic arch.
bone.zygomatic_bone.clinical: Fractures of the cheekbone complex can flatten the cheek and numb the cheek via the infra-orbital nerve.

bone.nasal_bone.name: Nasal bone
bone.nasal_bone.summary: Small paired bones forming the bony bridge of the nose.
bone.nasal_bone.clinical: The most commonly fractured facial bone.

bone.lacrimal_bone.name: Lacrimal bone
bone.lacrimal_bone.summary: The smallest facial bone, in the medial wall of the orbit. Helps form the fossa for the lacrimal sac.

bone.palatine_bone.name: Palatine bone
bone.palatine_bone.summary: L-shaped bone forming the posterior hard palate and parts of the nasal cavity wall and orbital floor.

bone.inferior_nasal_concha.name: Inferior nasal concha
bone.inferior_nasal_concha.summary: A separate scroll-shaped bone on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity. The nasolacrimal duct opens beneath it, into the inferior meatus.

bone.vomer.name: Vomer
bone.vomer.summary: Thin midline bone forming the posteroinferior part of the nasal septum.

bone.mandible.name: Mandible
bone.mandible.summary: The lower jaw, the only movable bone of the skull. Holds the lower teeth; its condyles form the temporomandibular joints. The mental foramen transmits the mental nerve and vessels.
bone.mandible.clinical: Commonly fractured, often in two places at once.

bone.hyoid_bone.name: Hyoid bone
bone.hyoid_bone.summary: U-shaped bone that does not articulate with any other bone. Suspended by muscles and ligaments, it anchors the tongue and the supra- and infrahyoid muscles.
bone.hyoid_bone.clinical: Fracture of the hyoid can be a forensic sign of strangulation.

bone.atlas_c1.name: Atlas (C1)
bone.atlas_c1.summary: First cervical vertebra. Has no body; it carries the skull, and the atlanto-occipital joints allow nodding.
bone.atlas_c1.clinical: A burst fracture of the atlas is called a Jefferson fracture.

bone.axis_c2.name: Axis (C2)
bone.axis_c2.summary: Second cervical vertebra. Its dens (odontoid process) is the pivot around which the atlas and skull rotate.
bone.axis_c2.clinical: Fractures of the dens are among the commonest cervical spine fractures in older people.

bone.major_alar_cartilage.name: Major alar cartilage
bone.major_alar_cartilage.summary: Shapes the tip of the nose and the margins of the nostrils.

bone.lateral_nasal_cartilage.name: Lateral process of septal cartilage
bone.lateral_nasal_cartilage.summary: Also called the upper lateral cartilage. Supports the middle third of the external nose, below the nasal bones.

bone.septal_cartilage.name: Septal nasal cartilage
bone.septal_cartilage.summary: Forms the anterior, cartilaginous part of the nasal septum.

bone.maxillary_teeth.name: Upper (maxillary) teeth
bone.maxillary_teeth.summary: Incisors, canines, premolars and first and second molars of the upper jaw (third molars are not modelled). Sensory supply from the superior alveolar nerves (maxillary nerve, V2).

bone.mandibular_teeth.name: Lower (mandibular) teeth
bone.mandibular_teeth.summary: Incisors, canines, premolars and first and second molars of the lower jaw (third molars are not modelled). Sensory supply from the inferior alveolar nerve (V3).

muscle.frontalis.name: Frontalis (frontal belly of occipitofrontalis)
muscle.frontalis.insertion: Skin of the eyebrows and forehead
muscle.frontalis.innervation: Temporal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.frontalis.action: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead
muscle.frontalis.blood: Supra-orbital and supratrochlear arteries; frontal branch of superficial temporal artery
muscle.frontalis.clinical: Spared in a stroke (upper motor neuron lesion) because of bilateral cortical control, but paralysed in Bell's palsy. Botulinum toxin is used to soften forehead lines.

muscle.occipitalis.name: Occipitalis (occipital belly of occipitofrontalis)
muscle.occipitalis.summary: Posterior belly of the scalp muscle.
muscle.occipitalis.origin: Lateral superior nuchal line and mastoid part of the temporal bone
muscle.occipitalis.innervation: Posterior auricular branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscle.temporoparietalis.name: Temporoparietalis
muscle.temporoparietalis.summary: Thin, variable muscle sheet of the scalp above the ear.
muscle.temporoparietalis.innervation: Temporal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscle.epicranial_aponeurosis.name: Epicranial aponeurosis
muscle.epicranial_aponeurosis.summary: Tough fibrous sheet covering the vault of the skull. It links the frontal and occipital bellies of occipitofrontalis and is one of the layers of the scalp.

muscle.procerus.name: Procerus
muscle.procerus.summary: Small muscle over the bridge of the nose.
muscle.procerus.origin: Fascia over the nasal bone and upper lateral nasal cartilage
muscle.procerus.action: Pulls the medial eyebrows down, making horizontal wrinkles over the bridge of the nose
muscle.procerus.clinical: A target for botulinum toxin to reduce horizontal lines at the root of the nose.

muscle.corrugator_supercilii.name: Corrugator supercilii
muscle.corrugator_supercilii.summary: Small muscle deep to the eyebrow.
muscle.corrugator_supercilii.origin: Medial end of the superciliary arch
muscle.corrugator_supercilii.insertion: Skin of the middle of the eyebrow
muscle.corrugator_supercilii.innervation: Temporal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.corrugator_supercilii.action: Draws the eyebrows medially and down (frowning)
muscle.corrugator_supercilii.clinical: A target for botulinum toxin to reduce vertical frown lines between the brows.

muscle.orbicularis_oculi_orbital.name: Orbicularis oculi – orbital part
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_orbital.summary: Outer ring of the sphincter around the eye.
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_orbital.origin: Nasal part of frontal bone, frontal process of maxilla, medial palpebral ligament
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_orbital.insertion: Encircles the orbit and returns near its origin
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_orbital.innervation: Temporal and zygomatic branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_orbital.blood: Branches of the facial, superficial temporal and ophthalmic arteries
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_orbital.clinical: Weakness (e.g. Bell's palsy) prevents full eye closure, so the cornea can dry out.

muscle.orbicularis_oculi_palpebral.name: Orbicularis oculi – palpebral part
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_palpebral.summary: Thin inner part of the sphincter, within the eyelids.
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_palpebral.innervation: Temporal and zygomatic branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_palpebral.blood: Branches of the facial, superficial temporal and ophthalmic arteries
muscle.orbicularis_oculi_palpebral.clinical: Weakness (e.g. Bell's palsy) stops the eye from closing fully during blinking.

muscle.nasalis.name: Nasalis
muscle.nasalis.summary: Muscle of the external nose with transverse and alar parts.
muscle.nasalis.origin: Maxilla, above the incisor and canine teeth
muscle.nasalis.insertion: Aponeurosis over the nasal dorsum and the alar cartilages
muscle.nasalis.innervation: Buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.nasalis.action: Compresses (transverse part) or flares (alar part) the nostrils

muscle.depressor_septi_nasi.name: Depressor septi nasi
muscle.depressor_septi_nasi.summary: Small muscle beneath the upper lip.
muscle.depressor_septi_nasi.insertion: Mobile part of the nasal septum
muscle.depressor_septi_nasi.innervation: Buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.depressor_septi_nasi.action: Pulls the tip of the nose down

muscle.levator_labii_superioris_alaeque_.name: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
muscle.levator_labii_superioris_alaeque_.latin: Musculus levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
muscle.levator_labii_superioris_alaeque_.summary: Labelled "levator nasolabialis" in the source model.
muscle.levator_labii_superioris_alaeque_.insertion: Alar cartilage and skin of the upper lip
muscle.levator_labii_superioris_alaeque_.innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.levator_labii_superioris_alaeque_.action: Elevates the upper lip and dilates the nostril

muscle.levator_labii_superioris.name: Levator labii superioris
muscle.levator_labii_superioris.summary: Flat muscle of the upper lip.
muscle.levator_labii_superioris.origin: Infra-orbital margin of the maxilla, above the infra-orbital foramen
muscle.levator_labii_superioris.insertion: Skin and muscle of the upper lip
muscle.levator_labii_superioris.innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscle.levator_anguli_oris.name: Levator anguli oris
muscle.levator_anguli_oris.summary: Lies deep to levator labii superioris.
muscle.levator_anguli_oris.origin: Canine fossa of the maxilla, below the infra-orbital foramen
muscle.levator_anguli_oris.innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.levator_anguli_oris.action: Elevates the angle of the mouth

muscle.zygomaticus_major.name: Zygomaticus major
muscle.zygomaticus_major.origin: Lateral surface of the zygomatic bone
muscle.zygomaticus_major.innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.zygomaticus_major.action: Draws the angle of the mouth upwards and laterally
muscle.zygomaticus_major.blood: Superior labial branch of the facial artery
muscle.zygomaticus_major.clinical: A genuine ("Duchenne") smile combines zygomaticus major with the orbital part of orbicularis oculi.

muscle.zygomaticus_minor.name: Zygomaticus minor
muscle.zygomaticus_minor.summary: Slender muscle medial to zygomaticus major.
muscle.zygomaticus_minor.innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscle.risorius.name: Risorius
muscle.risorius.summary: Thin, variable muscle of the cheek.
muscle.risorius.origin: Fascia over the parotid gland and masseter
muscle.risorius.innervation: Buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.risorius.action: Pulls the angle of the mouth laterally
muscle.risorius.blood: Superior labial branch of the facial artery

muscle.buccinator.name: Buccinator
muscle.buccinator.summary: Muscle forming the wall of the cheek. The parotid duct pierces it.
muscle.buccinator.origin: Alveolar processes of maxilla and mandible opposite the molars; pterygomandibular raphe
muscle.buccinator.insertion: Angle of the mouth, blending with orbicularis oris
muscle.buccinator.innervation: Buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.buccinator.action: Presses the cheek against the teeth, keeping food between them; used in blowing
muscle.buccinator.clinical: When paralysed, food collects between the cheek and the teeth.

muscle.orbicularis_oris.name: Orbicularis oris
muscle.orbicularis_oris.origin: Maxilla and mandible near the midline, and fibres from other muscles at the modiolus
muscle.orbicularis_oris.insertion: Skin and mucous membrane of the lips
muscle.orbicularis_oris.innervation: Buccal and marginal mandibular branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.orbicularis_oris.clinical: Weakness causes drooling and difficulty whistling or blowing.

muscle.depressor_anguli_oris.name: Depressor anguli oris
muscle.depressor_anguli_oris.summary: Triangular muscle below the corner of the mouth.
muscle.depressor_anguli_oris.innervation: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.depressor_anguli_oris.action: Pulls the angle of the mouth down (frowning)
muscle.depressor_anguli_oris.blood: Inferior labial branch of the facial artery

muscle.depressor_labii_inferioris.name: Depressor labii inferioris
muscle.depressor_labii_inferioris.summary: Quadrilateral muscle of the lower lip.
muscle.depressor_labii_inferioris.origin: Oblique line of the mandible, between the symphysis and mental foramen
muscle.depressor_labii_inferioris.innervation: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscle.mentalis.name: Mentalis
muscle.mentalis.innervation: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.mentalis.action: Raises and protrudes the lower lip; wrinkles the chin

muscle.platysma.name: Platysma
muscle.platysma.summary: Broad, thin sheet in the superficial fascia of the neck.
muscle.platysma.origin: Fascia over the upper pectoralis major and deltoid
muscle.platysma.insertion: Inferior border of the mandible, skin of the lower face and angle of the mouth
muscle.platysma.innervation: Cervical branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscle.platysma.action: Tenses the skin of the neck; helps depress the mandible and corner of the mouth

muscle.temporalis.name: Temporalis
muscle.temporalis.summary: Fan-shaped muscle filling the temporal fossa.
muscle.temporalis.origin: Floor of the temporal fossa and deep temporal fascia
muscle.temporalis.insertion: Coronoid process and anterior border of the ramus of the mandible
muscle.temporalis.action: Elevates the mandible; posterior fibres retract it
muscle.temporalis.blood: Deep temporal arteries (maxillary) and middle temporal artery (superficial temporal)
muscle.temporalis.clinical: Can be felt contracting at the temple when you clench your teeth.

muscle.masseter_superficial.name: Masseter – superficial part
muscle.masseter_superficial.summary: Larger, outer part of the masseter.
muscle.masseter_superficial.origin: Zygomatic process of maxilla and anterior two-thirds of the lower border of the zygomatic arch
muscle.masseter_superficial.insertion: Angle and lower lateral surface of the ramus of the mandible
muscle.masseter_superficial.blood: Masseteric artery (maxillary), transverse facial and facial arteries
muscle.masseter_superficial.clinical: Easily felt at the angle of the jaw when you clench your teeth; it may enlarge in people who grind their teeth.

muscle.masseter_deep.name: Masseter – deep part
muscle.masseter_deep.summary: Smaller, deeper part of the masseter.
muscle.masseter_deep.origin: Posterior third and deep surface of the zygomatic arch
muscle.masseter_deep.insertion: Upper lateral surface of the ramus and coronoid process
muscle.masseter_deep.action: Elevates and helps retract the mandible
muscle.masseter_deep.blood: Masseteric artery (maxillary), transverse facial and facial arteries

muscle.medial_pterygoid.name: Medial pterygoid
muscle.medial_pterygoid.summary: Quadrangular muscle on the inner side of the ramus, mirroring the masseter.
muscle.medial_pterygoid.origin: Medial surface of the lateral pterygoid plate; maxillary tuberosity
muscle.medial_pterygoid.insertion: Medial surface of the ramus near the angle of the mandible
muscle.medial_pterygoid.innervation: Nerve to medial pterygoid (mandibular nerve, V3)
muscle.medial_pterygoid.action: Elevates and protrudes the mandible; side-to-side grinding
muscle.medial_pterygoid.blood: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary artery

muscle.lateral_pterygoid_superior.name: Lateral pterygoid – superior head
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_superior.summary: Upper head of the lateral pterygoid.
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_superior.origin: Infratemporal surface of the greater wing of the sphenoid
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_superior.insertion: Capsule and articular disc of the temporomandibular joint, and neck of the mandible
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_superior.innervation: Nerve to lateral pterygoid (mandibular nerve, V3)
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_superior.action: Stabilises the disc and condyle, especially during closing
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_superior.blood: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary artery

muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.name: Lateral pterygoid – inferior head
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.summary: Lower head of the lateral pterygoid.
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid plate
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.insertion: Pterygoid fovea on the neck of the mandible
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.innervation: Nerve to lateral pterygoid (mandibular nerve, V3)
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.action: Protrudes the mandible and opens the jaw; side-to-side movement
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.blood: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary artery
muscle.lateral_pterygoid_inferior.clinical: The main jaw-opening muscle of mastication; the others close the jaw.

muscle.sternocleidomastoid.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscle.sternocleidomastoid.summary: Key landmark dividing the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.
muscle.sternocleidomastoid.origin: Manubrium of sternum (sternal head) and medial third of clavicle (clavicular head)
muscle.sternocleidomastoid.insertion: Mastoid process and lateral half of the superior nuchal line
muscle.sternocleidomastoid.action: One side: tilts the head to the same side and turns the face to the opposite side. Both sides: flex the neck
muscle.sternocleidomastoid.clinical: A shortened sternocleidomastoid in infants causes congenital muscular torticollis (head tilt).

muscle.digastric_anterior.name: Digastric – anterior belly
muscle.digastric_anterior.insertion: Intermediate tendon, attached to the hyoid bone
muscle.digastric_anterior.action: Depresses the mandible; elevates the hyoid

muscle.digastric_posterior.name: Digastric – posterior belly
muscle.digastric_posterior.summary: Suprahyoid muscle running from the mastoid region to the hyoid.
muscle.digastric_posterior.origin: Mastoid notch of the temporal bone
muscle.digastric_posterior.insertion: Intermediate tendon, attached to the hyoid bone
muscle.digastric_posterior.action: Elevates and retracts the hyoid; assists jaw opening

muscle.mylohyoid.name: Mylohyoid
muscle.mylohyoid.summary: Forms the muscular floor of the mouth.
muscle.mylohyoid.insertion: Midline raphe and body of the hyoid bone
muscle.mylohyoid.action: Elevates the hyoid and floor of the mouth (swallowing, speaking)
muscle.mylohyoid.blood: Mylohyoid branch of the inferior alveolar artery and submental artery

muscle.stylohyoid.name: Stylohyoid
muscle.stylohyoid.summary: Slender suprahyoid muscle; its tendon splits around the digastric tendon.
muscle.stylohyoid.origin: Styloid process of the temporal bone

muscle.levator_palpebrae_superioris.name: Levator palpebrae superioris
muscle.levator_palpebrae_superioris.origin: Lesser wing of the sphenoid, above the optic canal
muscle.levator_palpebrae_superioris.insertion: Skin and tarsal plate of the upper eyelid
muscle.levator_palpebrae_superioris.innervation: Oculomotor nerve (CN III); its smooth-muscle part (superior tarsal) is sympathetic
muscle.levator_palpebrae_superioris.blood: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery
muscle.levator_palpebrae_superioris.clinical: Oculomotor nerve palsy causes complete ptosis (drooping lid); Horner syndrome causes only partial ptosis via the smooth-muscle part.

muscle.superior_rectus.name: Superior rectus
muscle.superior_rectus.summary: One of the four rectus muscles of the eye.
muscle.superior_rectus.insertion: Superior sclera, in front of the equator
muscle.superior_rectus.action: Elevates the eye; also adducts and intorts it
muscle.superior_rectus.blood: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery

muscle.inferior_rectus.name: Inferior rectus
muscle.inferior_rectus.summary: One of the four rectus muscles of the eye.
muscle.inferior_rectus.insertion: Inferior sclera, in front of the equator
muscle.inferior_rectus.action: Depresses the eye; also adducts and extorts it

muscle.medial_rectus.name: Medial rectus
muscle.medial_rectus.blood: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery

muscle.lateral_rectus.name: Lateral rectus
muscle.lateral_rectus.summary: One of the four rectus muscles of the eye.
muscle.lateral_rectus.clinical: Abducens nerve palsy stops the eye turning outwards, giving horizontal double vision.

muscle.superior_oblique.name: Superior oblique
muscle.superior_oblique.summary: Its tendon runs through a pulley (the trochlea) before turning back to the eye.
muscle.superior_oblique.origin: Body of the sphenoid, above and medial to the optic canal
muscle.superior_oblique.action: Intorts, depresses and abducts the eye (depression is greatest when the eye is adducted)
muscle.superior_oblique.blood: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery
muscle.superior_oblique.clinical: Trochlear nerve palsy gives vertical double vision, worst when looking down (e.g. going downstairs).

muscle.inferior_oblique.name: Inferior oblique
muscle.inferior_oblique.summary: The only extra-ocular muscle arising from the front of the orbit.
muscle.inferior_oblique.origin: Orbital surface of the maxilla, in the floor of the orbit
muscle.inferior_oblique.action: Extorts, elevates and abducts the eye (elevation is greatest when the eye is adducted)

nerve.facial_nerve.name: Facial nerve (CN VII) – root & trunk
nerve.facial_nerve.summary: Leaves the brainstem, runs through the internal acoustic meatus and the facial canal of the temporal bone, exits at the stylomastoid foramen and enters the parotid gland, where it divides (the parotid plexus, or "pes anserinus") into five branches: temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular and cervical. Also carries taste and secretomotor fibres. In this model the piece includes the intracranial and intratemporal course plus two short twigs that are not labelled.
nerve.facial_nerve.supplies: Via its branches: muscles of facial expression, platysma, posterior belly of digastric, stylohyoid, stapedius
nerve.facial_nerve.clinical: Bell's palsy (idiopathic facial nerve palsy) weakens the whole of one side of the face, including the forehead; a stroke usually spares the forehead because of bilateral cortical input. The nerve runs through the parotid gland, between its superficial and deep parts, so it is at risk in parotid surgery.

nerve.chorda_tympani.name: Chorda tympani
nerve.chorda_tympani.summary: Crosses the middle ear next to the eardrum and joins the lingual nerve. Carries taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and secretomotor fibres to the submandibular and sublingual glands.
nerve.chorda_tympani.clinical: Can be stretched or cut during middle-ear surgery, altering taste on the front of the tongue.

nerve.trigeminal_nerve.name: Trigeminal nerve (CN V)
nerve.trigeminal_nerve.summary: The main sensory nerve of the face, and motor to the muscles of mastication. Divides at the trigeminal ganglion into ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2) and mandibular (V3) nerves.
nerve.trigeminal_nerve.clinical: Trigeminal neuralgia causes brief, severe electric-shock-like facial pain in its territory.

nerve.trigeminal_sensory_root.name: Sensory root of trigeminal nerve
nerve.trigeminal_sensory_root.summary: Large root carrying sensation from the face to the pons.

nerve.trigeminal_motor_root.name: Motor root of trigeminal nerve
nerve.trigeminal_motor_root.summary: Small root that joins the mandibular nerve to supply the muscles of mastication.

nerve.ophthalmic_nerve.name: Ophthalmic nerve (V1)
nerve.ophthalmic_nerve.summary: Enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure as the frontal, lacrimal and nasociliary nerves. Supplies the forehead, upper eyelid, cornea and dorsum of the nose.
nerve.ophthalmic_nerve.clinical: Shingles in this division (herpes zoster ophthalmicus) can threaten the eye.

nerve.maxillary_nerve.name: Maxillary nerve (V2)
nerve.maxillary_nerve.summary: Leaves the skull through the foramen rotundum and continues as the infra-orbital nerve. Supplies the lower eyelid, cheek, upper lip, upper teeth, palate and nasal cavity.
nerve.maxillary_nerve.clinical: Orbital floor fractures can damage its infra-orbital continuation, numbing the cheek and upper lip.

nerve.mandibular_nerve_anterior.name: Mandibular nerve (V3) – anterior division
nerve.mandibular_nerve_anterior.summary: Mainly motor: masseteric, deep temporal and lateral pterygoid nerves. Its one sensory branch is the buccal nerve.

nerve.mandibular_nerve_posterior.name: Mandibular nerve (V3) – posterior division
nerve.mandibular_nerve_posterior.summary: Mainly sensory: auriculotemporal, lingual and inferior alveolar nerves. Its motor branch is the nerve to mylohyoid.

nerve.buccal_nerve.name: Buccal nerve
nerve.buccal_nerve.summary: Sensory to the skin and mucous membrane of the cheek. It does not supply the buccinator muscle, which is supplied by the facial nerve.

nerve.lingual_nerve.name: Lingual nerve
nerve.lingual_nerve.summary: General sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, floor of the mouth and lingual gums. Carries chorda tympani fibres.
nerve.lingual_nerve.clinical: Lies close to the lower third molar and can be injured during its extraction, numbing the tongue.

nerve.inferior_alveolar_nerve.name: Inferior alveolar nerve
nerve.inferior_alveolar_nerve.summary: Enters the mandibular foramen and runs in the mandibular canal to supply the lower teeth. Anaesthetised in the dental "inferior alveolar nerve block".
nerve.inferior_alveolar_nerve.fibres: Sensory (gives off the motor nerve to mylohyoid)
nerve.inferior_alveolar_nerve.clinical: Blocked with local anaesthetic for lower dental work; can be injured during lower third-molar removal.

nerve.mental_nerve.name: Mental nerve
nerve.mental_nerve.summary: Terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve; emerges from the mental foramen to supply the skin of the chin and the lower lip.
nerve.mental_nerve.clinical: Damage numbs the lower lip and chin.

nerve.nerve_to_mylohyoid.name: Nerve to mylohyoid
nerve.nerve_to_mylohyoid.summary: Branch of the inferior alveolar nerve supplying mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric.

nerve.optic_nerve.name: Optic nerve (CN II)
nerve.optic_nerve.summary: Carries visual information from the retina through the optic canal to the optic chiasm.
nerve.optic_nerve.clinical: Swelling of the optic disc (papilloedema) is a sign of raised intracranial pressure.

nerve.oculomotor_nerve.name: Oculomotor nerve (CN III)
nerve.oculomotor_nerve.summary: Supplies the superior, inferior and medial recti, inferior oblique and levator palpebrae superioris; its parasympathetic fibres constrict the pupil and focus the lens.
nerve.oculomotor_nerve.clinical: A palsy gives a "down and out" eye, ptosis and often a dilated pupil (e.g. from an aneurysm pressing on it).

nerve.trochlear_nerve.name: Trochlear nerve (CN IV)
nerve.trochlear_nerve.summary: Supplies the superior oblique muscle. The only cranial nerve to leave the back of the brainstem.

nerve.abducens_nerve.name: Abducens nerve (CN VI)
nerve.abducens_nerve.summary: Supplies the lateral rectus muscle, which turns the eye outwards.
nerve.abducens_nerve.clinical: Its long intracranial course makes it vulnerable to raised intracranial pressure.

nerve.hypoglossal_nerve.name: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
nerve.hypoglossal_nerve.summary: Motor to the intrinsic and most extrinsic muscles of the tongue (all except palatoglossus).
nerve.hypoglossal_nerve.clinical: A lesion makes the protruded tongue deviate towards the weak side.

vessel.external_carotid_artery.name: External carotid artery
vessel.external_carotid_artery.summary: Branch of the common carotid artery that supplies the face, scalp and neck. It ends in the parotid gland by dividing into the maxillary and superficial temporal arteries.

vessel.internal_carotid_artery.name: Internal carotid artery
vessel.internal_carotid_artery.summary: Gives no branches in the neck. Enters the skull through the carotid canal to supply the brain, and the orbit via the ophthalmic artery.
vessel.internal_carotid_artery.clinical: Narrowing at its origin (carotid stenosis) is an important cause of stroke.

vessel.facial_artery.name: Facial artery
vessel.facial_artery.summary: Branch of the external carotid. Hooks over the mandible at the front of the masseter (where its pulse can be felt) and winds towards the medial corner of the eye.
vessel.facial_artery.clinical: Its pulse can be felt where it crosses the lower border of the mandible.

vessel.angular_artery.name: Angular artery
vessel.angular_artery.summary: Terminal part of the facial artery beside the nose; anastomoses with branches of the ophthalmic artery.

vessel.superior_labial_artery.name: Superior labial artery
vessel.superior_labial_artery.summary: Branch of the facial artery to the upper lip; joins its partner from the other side and sends branches to the nasal septum.

vessel.inferior_labial_artery.name: Inferior labial artery
vessel.inferior_labial_artery.summary: Branch of the facial artery to the lower lip.

vessel.submental_artery.name: Submental artery
vessel.submental_artery.summary: Branch of the facial artery running below the mandible to the chin and floor of the mouth.

vessel.superficial_temporal_artery.name: Superficial temporal artery
vessel.superficial_temporal_artery.summary: Terminal branch of the external carotid. Ascends in front of the ear, where its pulse can be felt, and supplies much of the scalp.
vessel.superficial_temporal_artery.clinical: Biopsied to diagnose giant cell (temporal) arteritis.

vessel.superficial_temporal_artery_front.name: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery
vessel.superficial_temporal_artery_front.summary: Supplies the scalp of the forehead; anastomoses with the supra-orbital and supratrochlear arteries.

vessel.transverse_facial_artery.name: Transverse facial artery
vessel.transverse_facial_artery.summary: Branch of the superficial temporal artery running across the face below the zygomatic arch, with the parotid duct.

vessel.maxillary_artery.name: Maxillary artery
vessel.maxillary_artery.summary: Larger terminal branch of the external carotid. Passes behind the neck of the mandible to supply the jaws, teeth, muscles of mastication, nasal cavity, palate and dura (via the middle meningeal artery).
vessel.maxillary_artery.clinical: Its sphenopalatine branch is the usual source of severe posterior nosebleeds.

vessel.inferior_alveolar_artery.name: Inferior alveolar artery
vessel.inferior_alveolar_artery.summary: Branch of the maxillary artery that runs with the inferior alveolar nerve in the mandibular canal to supply the lower teeth.

vessel.infraorbital_artery.name: Infra-orbital artery
vessel.infraorbital_artery.summary: Continuation of the maxillary artery through the floor of the orbit, emerging at the infra-orbital foramen.

vessel.occipital_artery.name: Occipital artery
vessel.occipital_artery.summary: Branch of the external carotid supplying the back of the scalp.

vessel.ophthalmic_artery.name: Ophthalmic artery
vessel.ophthalmic_artery.summary: First branch of the internal carotid inside the skull; enters the orbit through the optic canal and supplies the eye (including the retina) and orbit.

vessel.supraorbital_artery.name: Supra-orbital artery
vessel.supraorbital_artery.summary: Branch of the ophthalmic artery to the forehead and scalp.

vessel.supratrochlear_artery.name: Supratrochlear artery
vessel.supratrochlear_artery.summary: Terminal branch of the ophthalmic artery supplying the medial forehead.

vessel.facial_vein.name: Facial vein
vessel.facial_vein.summary: Main vein of the face, running behind the facial artery. Connects with the cavernous sinus through the ophthalmic veins, which is why infections around the nose and upper lip ("danger triangle") are taken seriously.

vessel.angular_vein.name: Angular vein
vessel.angular_vein.summary: Formed at the medial corner of the eye by the supratrochlear and supra-orbital veins; continues as the facial vein and communicates with the superior ophthalmic vein.

vessel.superior_labial_vein.name: Superior labial vein
vessel.superior_labial_vein.summary: Drains the upper lip into the facial vein.

vessel.inferior_labial_veins.name: Inferior labial veins
vessel.inferior_labial_veins.summary: Drain the lower lip into the facial vein.

vessel.submental_vein.name: Submental vein
vessel.submental_vein.summary: Drains the chin and floor of the mouth into the facial vein.

vessel.common_facial_vein.name: Common facial vein
vessel.common_facial_vein.summary: Short trunk formed by the facial vein and the anterior division of the retromandibular vein; drains into the internal jugular vein.

vessel.retromandibular_vein.name: Retromandibular vein
vessel.retromandibular_vein.summary: Formed in the parotid gland by the superficial temporal and maxillary veins. Divides into an anterior division (to the common facial vein) and a posterior division (to the external jugular vein).

vessel.superficial_temporal_veins.name: Superficial temporal veins
vessel.superficial_temporal_veins.summary: Drain the side of the scalp and join the maxillary vein to form the retromandibular vein.

vessel.internal_jugular_vein.name: Internal jugular vein
vessel.internal_jugular_vein.summary: Begins at the jugular foramen and runs in the carotid sheath. Drains the brain, face and neck, then joins the subclavian vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.
vessel.internal_jugular_vein.clinical: Common site for central venous catheters.

vessel.external_jugular_vein.name: External jugular vein
vessel.external_jugular_vein.summary: Formed near the angle of the mandible by the posterior auricular vein and the posterior division of the retromandibular vein; crosses sternocleidomastoid superficially to reach the subclavian vein.

vessel.posterior_auricular_vein.name: Posterior auricular vein
vessel.posterior_auricular_vein.summary: Drains the scalp behind the ear; helps form the external jugular vein.

organ.eyeball.name: Eyeball
organ.eyeball.summary: The globe of the eye. This model shows its outer coats: the white sclera, the transparent cornea and the iris.

organ.lacrimal_gland.name: Lacrimal gland
organ.lacrimal_gland.summary: Produces tears; sits in the upper outer part of the orbit. Its secretomotor supply comes from the facial nerve via the pterygopalatine ganglion.
organ.lacrimal_gland.clinical: Reduced tear secretion on the affected side can help localise a facial nerve lesion proximal to the geniculate ganglion.

organ.parotid_gland.name: Parotid gland
organ.parotid_gland.summary: The largest salivary gland, in front of and below the ear (model includes the accessory parotid). The facial nerve passes through it but does not supply it; its secretomotor fibres come from the glossopharyngeal nerve.
organ.parotid_gland.clinical: Swells in mumps. Most parotid tumours are benign (pleomorphic adenoma), but surgery must protect the facial nerve running through the gland.

organ.parotid_duct.name: Parotid duct
organ.parotid_duct.summary: Also called Stensen's duct. Crosses the masseter, pierces buccinator and opens into the mouth opposite the upper second molar.

organ.submandibular_gland.name: Submandibular gland
organ.submandibular_gland.summary: Salivary gland under the body of the mandible. Its duct opens beside the frenulum of the tongue; secretomotor supply via the chorda tympani and submandibular ganglion.

skin.frontal_region.name: Frontal region
skin.frontal_region.summary: Skin of the forehead, over the frontal bone (model includes the eyebrow).

skin.parietal_region.name: Parietal region
skin.parietal_region.summary: Skin of the top of the head, over the parietal bone.

skin.occipital_region.name: Occipital region
skin.occipital_region.summary: Skin at the back of the head, over the occipital bone.

skin.temporal_region.name: Temporal region
skin.temporal_region.summary: Skin of the temple, over the temporalis muscle.

skin.mastoid_region.name: Mastoid region
skin.mastoid_region.summary: Skin behind the ear, over the mastoid process.

skin.orbital_region.name: Orbital region
skin.orbital_region.summary: Skin around the eye, including the eyelids.

skin.infraorbital_region.name: Infra-orbital region
skin.infraorbital_region.summary: Skin below the eye, over the infra-orbital foramen.

skin.buccal_region.name: Buccal region
skin.buccal_region.summary: Skin of the cheek (model includes the nasolabial fold).

skin.parotideomasseteric_region.name: Parotid-masseteric region
skin.parotideomasseteric_region.summary: Skin over the parotid gland and masseter muscle.

skin.oral_region.name: Oral region
skin.oral_region.summary: Skin and red margin of the lips around the mouth (includes the philtrum and labial commissure).

skin.auricle.name: Auricle (external ear)
skin.auricle.summary: The visible ear: a cartilage framework covered by skin, including helix, antihelix, tragus, concha and lobule.

skin.submandibular_triangle.name: Submandibular triangle
skin.submandibular_triangle.summary: Area between the mandible and the two bellies of digastric; contains the submandibular gland.

skin.submental_triangle.name: Submental triangle
skin.submental_triangle.summary: Area under the chin between the anterior bellies of digastric and the hyoid.

skin.carotid_triangle.name: Carotid triangle
skin.carotid_triangle.summary: Area of the neck where the carotid pulse can be felt; bounded by sternocleidomastoid, posterior digastric and superior omohyoid.

skin.muscular_triangle.name: Muscular triangle
skin.muscular_triangle.summary: Lower front area of the neck, over the infrahyoid ("strap") muscles.

skin.lateral_region_of_neck.name: Lateral region of neck
skin.lateral_region_of_neck.summary: Also called the posterior triangle of the neck, behind sternocleidomastoid.

skin.posterior_region_of_neck.name: Posterior region of neck
skin.posterior_region_of_neck.summary: Skin of the back of the neck (nuchal region).

nerve.facial_temporal_branches.name: Temporal branches of facial nerve
nerve.facial_temporal_branches.summary: Leave the upper border of the parotid gland and cross the zygomatic arch to the temple and forehead.
nerve.facial_temporal_branches.supplies: Frontalis, upper orbicularis oculi, corrugator supercilii, anterior and superior auricular muscles
nerve.facial_temporal_branches.clinical: They lie superficially over the zygomatic arch, so they can be injured in arch fractures or temple/facelift surgery, causing an inability to raise the eyebrow on that side.

nerve.facial_zygomatic_branches.name: Zygomatic branches of facial nerve
nerve.facial_zygomatic_branches.summary: Run forwards across the zygomatic bone towards the lateral angle of the eye and the infra-orbital region.
nerve.facial_zygomatic_branches.supplies: Orbicularis oculi (especially its lower part), zygomaticus major and minor; share supply of the upper-lip elevators with the buccal branches
nerve.facial_zygomatic_branches.clinical: Injury weakens eye closure, which can leave the cornea exposed and dry.

nerve.facial_buccal_branches.name: Buccal branches of facial nerve
nerve.facial_buccal_branches.summary: Run forwards across the masseter, near the parotid duct, to the cheek, upper lip and nose. They form many interconnections with the zygomatic branches.
nerve.facial_buccal_branches.supplies: Buccinator, orbicularis oris, levator labii superioris (and alaeque nasi), levator anguli oris, risorius, nasalis, zygomaticus muscles
nerve.facial_buccal_branches.clinical: Because of their many cross-connections, an isolated buccal branch injury often recovers or is compensated. Buccinator weakness lets food collect in the cheek.

nerve.facial_marginal_mandibular_branch.name: Marginal mandibular branch of facial nerve
nerve.facial_marginal_mandibular_branch.summary: Runs forwards along the lower border of the mandible, deep to platysma, crossing superficial to the facial artery and vein.
nerve.facial_marginal_mandibular_branch.supplies: Depressor anguli oris, depressor labii inferioris, mentalis, lower orbicularis oris
nerve.facial_marginal_mandibular_branch.clinical: At risk in submandibular gland surgery and upper neck incisions, so incisions are placed well below the jaw. Injury gives an asymmetric smile: the lower lip on that side cannot be pulled down.

nerve.facial_cervical_branch.name: Cervical branch of facial nerve
nerve.facial_cervical_branch.summary: Leaves the lower pole of the parotid gland and descends into the neck beneath platysma.
nerve.facial_cervical_branch.clinical: Injury is usually minor, but because platysma helps pull down the corner of the mouth it can mimic marginal mandibular weakness ("pseudo-paralysis").

organ.frontal_sinus.name: Frontal sinus
organ.frontal_sinus.summary: Air space in the frontal bone above the orbits; drains into the middle meatus of the nose. Absent at birth, it develops during childhood.
organ.frontal_sinus.clinical: Can be involved in sinusitis, causing pain over the forehead.

organ.sphenoidal_sinus.name: Sphenoidal sinus
organ.sphenoidal_sinus.summary: Air space in the body of the sphenoid bone, directly below the pituitary fossa; drains into the sphenoethmoidal recess.
organ.sphenoidal_sinus.clinical: Surgeons can reach the pituitary gland through it (transsphenoidal surgery).

organ.ethmoidal_cells.name: Ethmoidal cells
organ.ethmoidal_cells.summary: Groups of small air cells in the ethmoid bone between the nose and the orbit (anterior, middle and posterior groups).
organ.ethmoidal_cells.clinical: Only a paper-thin plate of bone separates them from the orbit, so ethmoid sinusitis can spread to cause orbital cellulitis.

organ.tongue.name: Tongue
organ.tongue.summary: Muscular organ for taste, chewing, swallowing and speech.
organ.tongue.nerveSupply: Motor: hypoglossal nerve (CN XII), except palatoglossus (vagus). Anterior two-thirds: general sensation via the lingual nerve (V3), taste via the chorda tympani (CN VII). Posterior third: glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
organ.tongue.clinical: With a hypoglossal nerve lesion the protruded tongue deviates towards the weak side.

organ.sublingual_gland.name: Sublingual gland
organ.sublingual_gland.summary: The smallest major salivary gland, under the mucosa of the floor of the mouth; opens through many small ducts on the sublingual fold. Secretomotor supply via the chorda tympani and submandibular ganglion.

organ.lacrimal_sac.name: Lacrimal sac
organ.lacrimal_sac.summary: Upper dilated end of the tear-drainage system, in the lacrimal fossa at the medial corner of the orbit. Receives tears from the canaliculi.
organ.lacrimal_sac.clinical: Infection of the sac (dacryocystitis) causes a tender swelling beside the nose.

organ.nasolacrimal_duct.name: Nasolacrimal duct
organ.nasolacrimal_duct.summary: Carries tears from the lacrimal sac to the inferior meatus of the nose, which is why the nose runs when you cry.

muscle.geniohyoid.name: Geniohyoid
muscle.geniohyoid.origin: Inferior mental spine of the mandible
muscle.geniohyoid.innervation: C1 fibres carried by the hypoglossal nerve
muscle.geniohyoid.action: Pulls the hyoid forwards and up; helps depress the mandible

muscle.genioglossus.name: Genioglossus
muscle.genioglossus.summary: Fan-shaped extrinsic muscle forming the bulk of the tongue.
muscle.genioglossus.origin: Superior mental spine of the mandible
muscle.genioglossus.insertion: Dorsum of the tongue and body of the hyoid
muscle.genioglossus.clinical: With a hypoglossal nerve lesion the tongue deviates towards the weak side when protruded, because the healthy genioglossus pushes it across.

muscle.hyoglossus.name: Hyoglossus
muscle.hyoglossus.origin: Body and greater horn of the hyoid bone

vessel.middle_meningeal_artery.name: Middle meningeal artery
vessel.middle_meningeal_artery.summary: Branch of the maxillary artery that enters the skull through the foramen spinosum to supply the dura and skull bones.
vessel.middle_meningeal_artery.clinical: Its anterior branch runs deep to the pterion, where the skull is thin; a blow there can tear it, causing an extradural haematoma.

vessel.buccal_artery.name: Buccal artery
vessel.buccal_artery.summary: Branch of the maxillary artery that runs with the buccal nerve to the cheek and buccinator.

vessel.anterior_deep_temporal_artery.name: Anterior deep temporal artery
vessel.anterior_deep_temporal_artery.summary: Branch of the maxillary artery supplying the temporalis muscle.

vessel.posterior_deep_temporal_artery.name: Posterior deep temporal artery
vessel.posterior_deep_temporal_artery.summary: Branch of the maxillary artery supplying the temporalis muscle.

vessel.descending_palatine_artery.name: Descending palatine artery
vessel.descending_palatine_artery.summary: Branch of the maxillary artery that descends in the palatine canal and divides into the greater and lesser palatine arteries for the palate.

vessel.posterior_superior_alveolar_arter.name: Posterior superior alveolar artery
vessel.posterior_superior_alveolar_arter.summary: Branch of the maxillary artery supplying the upper molar and premolar teeth, gums and maxillary sinus.

vessel.mental_artery.name: Mental branch of inferior alveolar artery
vessel.mental_artery.summary: Leaves the mental foramen with the mental nerve to supply the chin and lower lip.

vessel.lacrimal_artery.name: Lacrimal artery
vessel.lacrimal_artery.summary: Branch of the ophthalmic artery supplying the lacrimal gland and eyelids.

vessel.ascending_pharyngeal_artery.name: Ascending pharyngeal artery
vessel.ascending_pharyngeal_artery.summary: Smallest branch of the external carotid; supplies the pharynx, prevertebral muscles, middle ear and meninges.

vessel.vertebral_artery.name: Vertebral artery
vessel.vertebral_artery.summary: Branch of the subclavian artery that climbs through the transverse foramina of the cervical vertebrae, enters the skull through the foramen magnum and joins its partner to form the basilar artery.

vessel.lingual_vein.name: Lingual vein
vessel.lingual_vein.summary: Drains the tongue into the internal jugular vein.

vessel.maxillary_veins.name: Maxillary veins
vessel.maxillary_veins.summary: Short veins from the pterygoid plexus that join the superficial temporal veins to form the retromandibular vein.

vessel.superior_ophthalmic_vein.name: Superior ophthalmic vein
vessel.superior_ophthalmic_vein.summary: Drains the orbit through the superior orbital fissure into the cavernous sinus; connects with the angular vein at the front.

vessel.inferior_ophthalmic_vein.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein
vessel.inferior_ophthalmic_vein.summary: Drains the floor of the orbit to the cavernous sinus and the pterygoid plexus.

vessel.transverse_sinus.name: Transverse sinus
vessel.transverse_sinus.summary: Runs from the confluence of sinuses along the attachment of the tentorium to become the sigmoid sinus.

vessel.sigmoid_sinus.name: Sigmoid sinus
vessel.sigmoid_sinus.summary: S-shaped sinus grooving the mastoid part of the temporal bone; continues as the internal jugular vein at the jugular foramen.
vessel.sigmoid_sinus.clinical: Because it lies next to the mastoid air cells, untreated mastoiditis can spread to it and cause sinus thrombosis.

vessel.cavernous_sinus.name: Cavernous sinus
vessel.cavernous_sinus.summary: Venous space on each side of the pituitary fossa. The internal carotid artery and abducens nerve run through it; the oculomotor, trochlear, ophthalmic and maxillary nerves lie in its lateral wall.
vessel.cavernous_sinus.clinical: Facial infections can spread here through the ophthalmic veins (cavernous sinus thrombosis), affecting the eye-movement nerves.

vessel.superior_sagittal_sinus.name: Superior sagittal sinus
vessel.superior_sagittal_sinus.summary: Runs along the upper margin of the falx cerebri; arachnoid granulations return cerebrospinal fluid into it. Drains to the confluence of sinuses.

vessel.straight_sinus.name: Straight sinus
vessel.straight_sinus.summary: Lies where the falx cerebri meets the tentorium; receives the inferior sagittal sinus and great cerebral vein and drains to the confluence of sinuses.

brain.cerebral_hemisphere.name: Cerebral hemisphere
brain.cerebral_hemisphere.summary: Frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes with the insula and limbic lobe. Each hemisphere mainly controls and senses the opposite side of the body. In this model the gyri are merged into one piece per side.

brain.cerebellum.name: Cerebellum
brain.cerebellum.summary: Coordinates movement, balance and posture, and contributes to motor learning.
brain.cerebellum.clinical: Damage causes clumsiness (ataxia) on the same side as the lesion.

brain.brainstem.name: Brainstem
brain.brainstem.summary: Midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata. Contains the nuclei of cranial nerves III–XII (the facial nerve nucleus is in the pons) and centres that control breathing and heart rate.

brain.corpus_callosum.name: Corpus callosum
brain.corpus_callosum.summary: The largest bundle of fibres connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.

brain.falx_cerebri.name: Falx cerebri
brain.falx_cerebri.summary: Sickle-shaped fold of dura mater between the cerebral hemispheres; the superior and inferior sagittal sinuses run along its edges.
